summary: Keep a running streak: it grows by 1 when today is warmer than yesterday and resets to 1 otherwise. Track the best streak seen (T6 — runs / streaks, using T5 neighbour comparison).

blocks.title: Read the temperatures
blocks.text: N on its own line, then N numbers on one line.

blocks.title: Start at 1, not 0
blocks.text: A single day already counts as a streak of 1, so both `best` and `cur` start at 1. Starting at 0 would print 0 for N = 1.

blocks.title: Warmer than yesterday → the streak grows
blocks.text: `i` starts at 1 so `t[i - 1]` is a real day. Strictly `>` — an equal day breaks the streak.

blocks.title: Otherwise restart
blocks.text: The streak starts over at 1 — today itself is the first day of the new streak.

blocks.title: Update the best every day
blocks.text: Doing this inside the loop (not only when a streak breaks) makes sure a streak that runs to the very last day is counted.

complexity: Time O(N) with N ≤ 10⁵ → 100,000 steps, instant.
pitfalls: Updating `best` only when the streak breaks — misses a streak at the end.
